channel.description: Latest articles from Coalition for a Prosperous America – Bias and Credibility (prosperousamerica.org)

item.title: AI Data Centers Help Drive January Goods Deficit of $81.7 Billion | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: The overall goods and services deficit number for January looked pretty good – coming in at $54.4 billion, its lowest monthly point in years. But when services are stripped from the equation, the goods trade looks like it has returned to level footing. January’s goods deficit was $81.7 billion, according to Thursday’s trade data from the Bureau of Economic Analysis.

item.title: CPA Commends Trump Administration for Launching Section 301 Investigations Targeting Global Manufacturing Overcapacity, Forced Labor | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: Section 301 is a powerful tool for addressing foreign policies that distort global markets and disadvantage American producers. When foreign governments explicitly pursue overproduction and then export the resulting surplus into the United States, the effect is to displace domestic output and deter new investment in American manufacturing.

item.title: New CPA Economic Model Answers Sen. Warren’s Request; Moves Modeling Closer to Reality | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: The development of GTAP-USL economic model marks another step forward in our efforts to make the GTAP more realistic and a better predictor of the real-world effects of trade policies or trade shocks. It’s critical to build models that provide a better understanding of how policies impact people, families, racial groups, gender, cities and regions. There is still more work to be done.

item.title: To Reduce the Deficit, Tariff the Money | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: To reduce the deficit in a durable way, the United States must do more than tariff goods. It must tariff the money.

item.title: Sen. Gillibrand Says U.S. Generics Need Incentives to Reshore; Cost Shouldn’t Trump Quality | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: It’s the second month in a row now that the U.S. Senate Special Committee on Aging has taken up the question of our woeful generics supply chain. This time, however, Ranking Member Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), started the hearing off by touching on a key topic in pharmaceuticals: the cost equation can no longer override the quality equation.

item.title: CPA Applauds Bipartisan Senate Letter Supporting Section 232 Polysilicon Investigation | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: The letter underscores a critical point: any effective policy response must address the entire solar supply chain—from polysilicon to ingots, wafers, cells, and finished modules—rather than focusing on a single segment in isolation.

item.title: Should Chinese Nationals Be Allowed to Donate to American Colleges, Participate in Research Grants? | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: Should Chinese organizations and individuals be allowed to donate to American colleges, and should their PhD students have access to scientific research grants? It’s not an easy question to answer.

item.title: CPA Applauds Bipartisan Senate Banking Committee Letter Urging SEC to Crack Down on China’s Exploitation of U.S. Capital Markets | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: This bipartisan letter from the Senate Banking Committee is a powerful signal that Congress is finally taking seriously what CPA has been warning about for years: the Chinese Communist Party has been exploiting America’s capital markets to fund its military modernization, underwrite its surveillance state, and enrich entities engaged in genocide, forced labor, and espionage — all with American investor capital.

item.title: New CPA–Responsible Battery Coalition Report Warns China’s Dominance of Battery Processing is a Threat to U.S. National Security | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: The report finds that China has consolidated global dominance in the midstream stages of battery supply chains—refining and chemical conversion—giving the Chinese Communist Party significant influence over pricing, supply availability, and industrial investment.

item.title: In House Hearing, Unanimous Agreement on China Risks in American Rx Supply | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: Everyone agrees, in particular that reliance on China for key ingredients used to make medicines is risky; and everyone agrees that further up market – in advanced biotech – China is becoming an unmatched rival that could easily shrink America’s role in drug innovation.

item.title: For China Commission, Warnings and Advice For Trump’s “Donroe Doctrine” in Latin America | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: Last November, the White House released its National Security Strategy of the United States that laid out the Trump administration’s strategy for the Americas. item.title: New Fed Research Backs CPA's Case on China's Industrial Policy and Record Surplus | Coalition For A Prosperous America
item.description: A new Federal Reserve FEDS Note finds a systematic link between Chinese industrial policy interventions and export growth. The 15 most policy-targeted sectors accounted for 76% of the increase in China's aggregate trade surplus from 2017 to 2024.
